newsitem.title: USA: US food aid may boost Cargill, N.Korea talks.
newsitem.headline: US food aid may boost Cargill, N.Korea talks.

text.p: Long-running talks between Cargill Inc. and North Korea to arrange financing for grain purchases may have received an indirect boost Wednesday, when the State Department's announced an extra $10 million in U.S. food aid for the famine-stricken nation.

Cargill spokesperson Lori Johnson said that, while it was difficult to speculate on the impact of the food aid decision on Cargill's discussions with North Korea, the announcement was a positive development overall.
"From a larger perspective beyond us, I think it's a good sign that things are moving along in a positive direction," Johnson said.

Cargill and North Korean officials have been negotiating for several weeks now on how to finance a 500,000 tonne sale of wheat and/or rice to the communist nation that was approved by the U.S. government in early January.

North Korea has reportedly asked for financing from the U.S. government -- which Washington said it would not provide for the commercial deal -- and Cargill reportedly has been receptive a barter arrangement.
Cargill has said it is looking at different options, but would not provide any details.
In an interview with Reuters Wednesday, Johnson said talks are still continuing and that the company is hopeful an agreement will be reached.
"I don't think it's unexpected that it would take some time... We're still optimistic," she said. "We're in about the same postiion we have been in for some time," she added.
Johnson said that although the negotiations are currently not being carried out face-to-face, she said Cargill officials are expected to go to North Korea before any deal is signed.
